To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used two methods, one using P elements and the other using FRTs, to generate a collection of deletions that cover most of the genome and have well-defined endpoints, and we have made these deletions available to the community.
we have generated a set of targeted deletions that are useful in the study of Drosophila development and function.

(1) a set of deletions with molecular endpoints has been generated that provides high-resolution coverage of the D. melanogastrer genome and (2) a set of targeted deletions has been generated that increases overall genomic coverage by approximately 5–7%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a set of high-resolution deletion lines in the D. melangoster genome.
the systematic generation and analysis of deletion coverage of the entire genome of Drosophila.
the systematic generation of deletions in Drosophila and with the development of a comprehensive set of tools for the systematic isolation and mapping of mutations in DrosophILA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion collections described here are a major advance in Drosophila genetics, and will greatly enhance the ability to map and characterize mutations in Drosophia.

the deletion collections described in this paper and the accompanying paper will provide the Drosophilist community with the most comprehensive and detailed collection of isogenic, genetically stable deletions with precisely defined endpoints that have ever been generated.

the two methods described here will provide the DrosophILA community with a set of high-quality deletions that will be useful to a variety of researchers and that the availability of these deletions will significantly increase our ability to study Drosophila genetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined efforts of these two projects have generated 1,200 isogenic, molecularly defined deletions with high resolution coverage of 62% of the D. melanoga ster genome.
we have generated 2,000 deletions in Drosophila, 1,000 by P -element and 1,000 with FRT.

the two deletion collections described here provide 61% genome coverage and that the second collection provides a powerful resource for the systematic generation of isogenic deletions in the fruit fly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the generation of deletions is no longer limited to the hands of a few experts and that the systematic generation of deletions will be an important tool to facilitate the analysis of complex phenotypes.
, with the availability of the complete genome sequence and the tools of modern molecular genetics, the systematic isolation of deletions is now possible.
the systematic generation of targeted deletions can be accomplished in a high-throughput fashion and will provide an important resource for Drosophila research.
